newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mixed, sterling skids.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mixed, sterling skids.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended pit trading mixed, with sterling skidding to huge daily losses in suddenly brisk trading near the close.

Analysts, economists and floor brokers each cited a news wire report from London saying an unnamed senior U.K. Labour source said U.K. membership in the ERM would be more attractive if sterling were closer to the 2.50 mark level.
The story jolted sterling futures into fast-market conditions as June triggered large sellstops on its descent.
The story's impact surprised some market watchers, who saw little surprising in the story's content.
"I'm surprised they reacted so strongly," said Earl Johnson, foreign exchange economist, Bank of Montreal in Chicago, as sterling slumped outright and in the mark cross.
Most other units shaved their gains late, after earlier re-approaching session peaks and again failing to follow through, floor brokers said.

The market reacted little to the Federal Reserve's Beige book of economic activity. The Fed said the nation's economy grew at a moderate rate through March and April and that U.S. wage and retail price pressures generally remained subdued.
Johnson said the Beige Book revealed little unexpected.
Lisa Finstrom, currency analyst, Smith Barney, also saw limited response to the Beige Book, which she called "mixed."

"The language seemed to be pretty full of potential inflationary threats," she said. In the short term, the expectation that inflation would lead to higher U.S. rates could be construed as dollar-supportive. But in the long term, she added, "it's not so hot."

Futures had firmed early, led by yen, on edginess about an overnight Japanese wire service report quoting an international monetary source as saying Japan, Germany and the United States were exploring the possibility of intervention.
A Bank of Japan official and a Bundesbank spokesman both declined comment on the report.
Sterling barely weakened early following Tuesday's rally and on weaker than expected U.K. March industrial output figures.

June yen ended up $0.000016 at $0.008045, marks firmed $0.0008 to $0.5831, Swiss francs added $0.0004 to $0.6878, sterling slid $0.0192 to $1.6176, Canadian dollar lost $0.0025 to $0.7256, Aussie dollar edged up $0.0002 to $0.7767, and Mexican peso fell $0.000675 to $0.123975.
